caption: Brendan Ngwa Nforbi v. Home Depot U.S.A., Inc.
court: USDC E.D. Cal. — Sacramento Division (proposed direct filing)
status: FEDERAL REDRAFT — 12(b)(6)-engineered E.D. Cal. complaint now affirmatively pleads on information and belief that Home Depot used Plaintiff's § 290.46 information for employment. UPS/FedEx First Advantage comparators are pleaded as factual support, not as substitutes for Home Depot's report.
note: The September 8, 2026 San Joaquin packet is historical work product only; it never reached the clerk. Federal review draft lives at internal/docs/matter-37/EDCA_FEDERAL_COMPLAINT_REVIEW_DRAFT.md. Public-source memo at internal/docs/matter-37/FIRST_ADVANTAGE_HOME_DEPOT_PUBLIC_SOURCE_MEMO.md supports pleading First Advantage as Home Depot's CRA on I&B and strengthens FCRA willfulness. Do not treat another employer's report as Home Depot's report. Exact discovery date remains a filing gate.
defendants: Home Depot U.S.A., Inc. is the proposed sole opening defendant as employer/user of the report. First Advantage Background Services Corp. is pleaded as Home Depot's CRA on information and belief based on Home Depot-branded federal-court exhibits, separate federal litigation, and First Advantage public screening materials; it remains a nonparty discovery source unless Home Depot-specific records support an independent CRA claim.
causes: [FEDERAL ANCHOR] FCRA, 15 U.S.C. § 1681b(b)(3)(A) — Home Depot allegedly took adverse employment action based in whole or in part on the First Advantage report without first providing the report and written Summary of Rights; negligent/willful remedies under §§ 1681o/1681n.

[DISTINCT STATE OMISSION] ICRAA, Civ. Code §§ 1786.40 and 1786.50 — upon denying/ending employment under circumstances in which an investigative report was obtained, Home Depot allegedly failed to advise Plaintiff and supply the CRA name/address. Pleaded as a different omission from the FCRA pre-adverse failure to avoid § 1786.52(a) same-act duplication.

[REPORT-CONDITIONED] Penal Code § 290.46(j)(2)(E), (j)(4)(A) — strongest version requires Home Depot-specific First Advantage report to identify California-registry-sourced information and show Home Depot used the report for the Tracy employment decision.
[OMITTED] UCL — limited remedial upside and unnecessary federal standing/remedy side fight.
[OMITTED] CCRAA — reserve unless the actual Home Depot product is an ordinary consumer credit report rather than an investigative employment report.
[OMITTED] Tameny / IIED — approximate August 2024 adverse-action date creates facial two-year limitations problems.
[RESERVED] FCRA § 1681b(b)(2)(A), Fair Chance Act / FEHA, and First Advantage vendor claims — add only if the actual forms, exhaustion record, or CRA conduct support them.
key_facts: Home Depot accepted Plaintiff for the Tracy operation, began onboarding, ran an employment background check, and then stopped the employment. Public records support First Advantage as Home Depot's CRA. The complaint now alleges as ultimate facts on I&B that First Advantage furnished Home Depot Plaintiff's § 290.46 information and Home Depot used it for the employment decision. Factual basis includes Plaintiff's contemporaneous California registry listing, UPS's First Advantage report on the same Plaintiff showing California-registry sourcing as the adverse/decisional component, FedEx's admission that its First Advantage report identified Plaintiff as a California registrant, and Home Depot's cessation of onboarding after the screen.
procedural_status: Pre-filing federal redraft on branch matter37-edca-federal-redraft-v2 / draft PR #795. Prior signed San Joaquin complaint/intake dated September 8, 2026 were never filed. Proposed forum is E.D. Cal., Sacramento, based on FCRA federal-question jurisdiction plus supplemental California claims. Public research materially upgrades the First Advantage vendor allegation and FCRA willfulness theory, but does not prove the contents of Plaintiff's report. Filing gates remain the true discovery date, DOT-exception check, correct Home Depot entity, and a final hostile audit of every I&B allegation.
damages: Federal draft seeks nonduplicative actual/compensatory damages including lost employment compensation; FCRA remedies under §§ 1681n/1681o; ICRAA actual damages or $10,000, whichever is greater, plus punitive damages if the statutory showing is met; and remedies authorized by Penal Code § 290.46(j)(4)(A). No wage rate or duration is presently fixed in the record. No civil-penalty-only valuation is assumed.
risk: Primary filing risk remains limitations: the true FCRA/ICRAA discovery date must be pleaded accurately. Merits pleading is now stronger: First Advantage vendor identity is supported by public Home Depot records, and § 290.46 source/use are pleaded as ultimate facts on I&B with UPS/FedEx same-consumer comparator support. Exact source wording, adjudication codes, access logs, and reason codes are reserved for discovery.
evidence: Plaintiff's statement — accepted Home Depot Tracy hire/onboarding; employment background check; employment then stopped

Ford v. Home Depot U.S.A., Inc., S.D. Cal. 3:19-cv-00754, Dkt. 1 Ex. 1 — Home Depot-branded California disclosure identifies First Advantage as the CRA Home Depot will use and states pre-adverse report/Summary-of-Rights process
Bolton v. First Advantage LNS Screening Solutions, Inc., S.D.N.Y. 1:14-cv-05735, July 1, 2015 opinion — recounts First Advantage report furnished to prospective employer Home Depot
First Advantage Dec. 4, 2019 workforce-screening announcement featuring a Home Depot representative
Later publicly indexed THD / First Advantage reports and applicant accounts — corroborative continuity evidence only; not primary pleading proof
Home Depot-specific First Advantage report/order/access/adjudication file — target discovery; exact contents and source fields not yet known
E.D. Cal. Local Rule 120(d) — San Joaquin County civil actions commence on the Sacramento side
